one_sentence: From minute 50 the play swung into Northgate's half, Harbour City's wide forwards went almost missing from the ball and Joss Draper had three close-range shots that were all saved, but nothing in the data, such as a tactical change, a fatigue spike or a substitution, clearly explains why.
evidence: Attacking position of play (mean event x, own attack direction): Harbour City 67.9 before (35-49) vs 36.7 after (50-64); Northgate 30.5 vs 57.5
Shots and xG, 35-49 vs 50-64: Harbour City 8 shots, xG 0.81 vs 1 shot, xG 0.11; Northgate 1 shot, xG 0.04 vs 4 shots, xG 0.68
Every outfield player moved by the same amount at minute 50 (Northgate +13.7 m, Harbour City +13.1 m, mean x), so the shape between the teams did not change
Mean speed: Northgate 11.27 to 10.91 km/h, Harbour City 11.64 to 11.23 km/h (change -0.36 and -0.41); largest single drop B8 -1.49 km/h, within the spread of A4 -1.15 and A8 -1.11
Harbour City forwards B9, B10, B11 touches fell from 71 (25-49) to 7 (50-64), while their completed passes stayed at 55 to 63 per team
alternatives_ruled_out: Substitution: the first substitution is at minute 63 (B7 off, B13 on), 13 minutes after the onset; no substitution happens at minute 50
Card: Harbour City's yellow to B6 at minute 47 is 3 minutes before the onset, and pressure flags, speed and position steps all change at minute 50 rather than 47
Player fatigue: speed fell by a similar amount for both teams (-0.36 vs -0.41 km/h), and B8's drop is z = -1.8 among 20 outfield players, not a clear outlier

Single player behaviour change: no outfield player's position moved relative to his teammates at minute 50, and Joss Draper's touches rose from 3 to 14 alongside a general rise in Northgate's receivers
Pressure: under-pressure flags fell from 28 to 2 for both teams at minute 50, which points to a change in the flow of play rather than one team pressing differently
